newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BTNZ recommends inflation-indexed bonds.
newsitem.headline: BTNZ recommends inflation-indexed bonds.

text.p: A recent rally in inflation-indexed bonds will be sustained because the bonds have been re-rated by international investors, Bankers Trust New Zealand said on Tuesday.
A total of NZ$50 million of the bonds will be tendered on Thursday. BTNZ said they would represent good value between 4.9 percent and five percent.
There are $374 million of the bonds currently on issue. They were trading at 5.03 percent in Tuesday's session.
BTNZ said the bonds have rallied 75 basis points since the last tender on September 26 and this had coincided with rallies in Canadian and Australian index-bond markets.
The bonds have returned 10.9 percent since the last tender compared with a return of 7.7 percent on November 2006 bonds.
Meanwhile, the spread of conventional bonds over inflation-indexed bonds has fallen slightly, from 2.31 percent to 2.12 percent despite indications that inflationary expectations have gone up.

BTNZ said gains in New Zealand inflation-indexed bonds would be sustained. It said political uncertainty and the prospect of a wider Reserve Bank inflation target made the bonds more attractive to investors.
Investors internationally were focusing on the sector and those who held the securities were reluctant to sell because they were limited in supply.
The bonds were strongly bid in the last tender with bids totalling $293 million received for the $50 million on offer. The successful bids fell in a range between 5.50 and 5.79 percent.
